challenges.name: typed-api-layer-quiz
challenges.title: Types at the boundary and exhaustive errors
challenges.description: Two pieces of the catalog's data layer: the old fetch that casts the response, and the new error union with an exhaustive switch. Decide whether each statement is True or False.

questions.explanation: False. `as CoursePage` is a type assertion: it tells the compiler to trust you and adds no runtime check. Types are erased when TypeScript compiles to JavaScript, so this course with level "Beginner" reaches the components unchanged, and a filter or a switch on level silently misses it. The fix is to treat the parsed body as unknown and check it with a type guard (or a schema validator) once, at the API boundary. The misconception is that static types, or --strict, validate data that arrives over the network.

True. Each case narrows error by its kind. With four cases for five variants, the value that reaches default is narrowed to { kind: "conflict"; message: string }, and passing it where never is expected is a compile error (Argument of type ... is not assignable to parameter of type 'never'). That is the point of the pattern: a new variant makes every switch that forgot it fail the build, instead of the UI quietly falling back to a generic message. The misconception is that assertNever is only a runtime guard; its main value is the compile-time check.

challenges.name: typed-api-result
challenges.title: Map every response to an ApiResult
challenges.description:
The catalog calls GET /api/courses through the new shared/api client. Write toApiResult(raw), which turns what the fetch wrapper saw into ApiResult<CoursePage>, and describeError(error), the message the catalog shows. The test runner reads one raw response as JSON ({ networkError, status, contentType, body, retryAfter? }; body is the response text) and prints { ok: true, total, ids } or { ok: false, error, message }.

toApiResult, the first matching rule wins:
1. networkError true -> { kind: "network" }.
2. Status 200-299: the content type without parameters (";charset=..."), trimmed and lowercased, must be "application/json" and the body must parse with JSON.parse, otherwise { kind: "bad_response", status, reason: "not_json" }; the parsed value must be a CoursePage, otherwise { kind: "bad_response", status, reason: "invalid_shape" }; then { ok: true, data }.
3. 401 -> unauthorized, 403 -> forbidden, 404 -> not_found.
4. 422 -> { kind: "validation", fieldErrors }: if the body is JSON (same content-type rule) and an object whose errors property is an object (not null, not an array), fieldErrors holds its entries whose value is a string, in order; otherwise {}.
5. 429 -> { kind: "rate_limited", retryAfter }: raw.retryAfter when it is an integer >= 0, otherwise null.
6. 500-599 -> { kind: "server", status }.
7. Any other status (1xx, 3xx, 400, 409, ...) -> { kind: "bad_response", status, reason: "unexpected_status" }: the client has no rule for it.

A CoursePage has items (an array of Course) and total (an integer >= 0). A Course has id and title (strings), level ("beginner", "intermediate" or "advanced"), tags (array of strings), rating (number from 0 to 5), learners (integer >= 0) and updatedAt (string); extra properties are allowed. One invalid course makes the whole page invalid.

describeError returns exactly the messages listed in the starter, as a switch on error.kind that ends in the provided assertNever. Do not change the types, assertNever or the test runner. The program is compiled with tsc --strict.
hints: What does the client know for certain about a response before it reads the body, and what can only be trusted after a check? Which of the test inputs would make a plain JSON.parse(raw.body) throw?

Split the work into small functions: one that returns the parsed body or "not JSON" (content type first, then JSON.parse inside try/catch), a type guard isCourse(value: unknown): value is Course, and isCoursePage built on it with items.every(isCourse). toApiResult then only decides by status, in the order of the rules. In describeError, every case returns, and default passes error to assertNever.

The same pattern for a different endpoint: GET /api/users/me returns { id: string, displayName: string, exp: number }. A guard isProfile(value: unknown) checks typeof value === "object" && value !== null, then typeof value.id === "string", typeof value.displayName === "string" and Number.isInteger(value.exp). For { "id": "u1", "displayName": "Lan", "exp": "1200" } it returns false (exp is a string), so the client answers bad_response with reason invalid_shape instead of letting "1200" + 50 become "120050" in the header.
